headless.source: Codex headless lane 2026-10-31 from the installed `codex exec --help` (codex-cli 0.166.0) and learn.chatgpt.com docs read 2026-10-31 (docs/non-interactive-mode, docs/developer-commands, docs/config-file/config-reference; the pages carry no date): one `codex exec` turn, read-only sandbox, approvals never, no persisted session, user config and execpolicy rules ignored, every documented tool switch off (shell, unified exec, web search, view_image, apps, multi-agent, remote plugins, hooks, memories, skills), built-in instructions replaced by the system prompt file. No toggle for apply_patch is documented: the line guard refuses any tool item, the sandbox is read-only and the realm writes only the run dir and the login dir. --strict-config is documented for config.toml fields only; the -c switches reduce, the line guard enforces. No model call was made. r2 (HL lane 2026-10-31, owner S12 probe: the exact argv, an empty CODEX_HOME, bwrap --unshare-net, no login): 0.166.0 --strict-config refused `tools.view_image` ('unknown configuration field `tools.view_image` in -c/--config override', exit 1, no JSON line: the WALK21 unknown calls); openai/codex rust-v0.166.0 codex-rs/core/config.schema.json ToolsToml has no view_image and codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs names the stable feature `view_image` (the config-reference page still lists tools.view_image), so the switch is features.view_image; every other -c key here was refused only for a bad value (known field).

login.source: Codex headless lane 2026-10-31 from learn.chatgpt.com/docs/developer-commands (read 2026-10-31): `codex login` signs in with ChatGPT in the browser (--device-auth = device code, --with-api-key reads a key: neither is used). guards.reconnectSource: HL lane 2026-10-31 (lead decision): `codex exec --json` reports the CLI's own stream retries as error lines 'Reconnecting... <n>/<max> (<cause>)' (owner S12 probe capture proof/ALPHA60/PAKET-2/HL/probe/2-without-tools-view-image.stdout.txt; openai/codex rust-v0.166.0 codex-rs/core/src/responses_retry.rs notify_stream_error, the first websocket retry hidden in release builds; codex-rs/model-provider-info/src/lib.rs DEFAULT_STREAM_MAX_RETRIES = 5). Such a line is a transient notice, counted up to maxReconnects (the CLI default; a WebSockets-to-HTTPS fallback restarts the CLI's count, so a longer run is refused); the unbounded 'Reconnecting... waiting for network' form, any other error line and turn.failed stay refusals.
guards.source: Codex headless lane 2026-10-31: item types from learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode (agent messages, reasoning, command executions, file changes, MCP tool calls) and the pinned SDK items the worker normalizer reads (web_search, todo_list, error); only the answer and its reasoning are allowed. Login patterns are unsourced (fail-closed: an unmatched error item is invalid output); quota patterns are providers.json quotaPolicy.codexPatterns. The retained worker stream shows an error item about hook timeouts before the turn: hooks are off here, and any error item still refuses.

isolation.source: bubblewrap 0.13.0 bwrap.xml (the bundled locked build's own manual source, read 2026-10-23): --unshare-all, --unshare-user, --disable-userns (requires --unshare-user), --die-with-parent, --proc, --dev, --size + --tmpfs, --perms, --ro-bind, --ro-bind-try, --bind, --chdir. No --share-net: the network namespace stays empty and only the gateway socket leads out. No --new-session: the runner's detached spawn already starts a session without a controlling terminal, and the process group must reach the CLI so SIGINT ends the turn first. S3-5 lane.

Every other existing entry is masked. Unmeasured against the real CLI until the lead's run.

refreshLock.source: f5 lane 2026-10-24: names from configVisible (S3-5, CLI 2.1.309 strings); none exists at rest and none appeared during in-realm --version, --help and auth status (names-only watch of the login dir). The realm binds the login dir itself, so the CLI's lock file is the same inode for the realm and the person's own sessions; whether the CLI's stale-lock check uses a process id is unverified, and the realm's own PID namespace would break such a check both ways. Deckent therefore starts no spawn while a CLI lock name exists, and serializes its own spawns per login dir (staleMs: a holder older than this is stale even if its process id was reused).

limits.boundsSource: f5 lane 2026-10-24, measured in this realm with the real CLI 2.1.309 (Bun 1.4.4; --help and auth status only, no model call): peak RSS 180 MB, CPU 0.12 s, 8 realm tasks; RLIMIT_NPROC counts the realm's own user namespace on kernel 6.18 (7 runs auth status while the owner has hundreds of processes; 5 aborts), Bun sizes its reservations to RLIMIT_DATA (512 MiB runs --help; 256 MiB aborts); prlimit adds no measurable time (--help 98-104 ms either way). Per process: CPU soft 60 s (SIGXCPU) and hard +5 s (SIGKILL), data 2 GiB; realm: 64 tasks. Turn-time peaks unmeasured until the lead's real call.
